seo.title: Become a Cloud Solution Architect | Free Roadmap for Engineers | Rupesh Tiwari
seo.description: Your complete roadmap to becoming a Cloud Solution Architect at FAANG companies. No algorithms required. No IIT degree needed. Start from basics and land your dream job.

hero.title: You CAN Become a Solution Architect
hero.subtitle: No algorithms. No IIT degree. No excuses.
hero.description: Think FAANG is only for IIT toppers? Think again. I've helped engineers from service companies, tier-2 colleges, and non-CS backgrounds land Solution Architect roles at AWS, Google, Microsoft, and more. Here's your complete roadmap.

mythBusters.title: Breaking the Myths
mythBusters.subtitle: What's really stopping you isn't what you think

myths.reality: I've coached engineers from tier-3 colleges, vernacular medium schools, and service companies who now work at Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. Your background doesn't define your future.

myths.myth: I need to master Data Structures & Algorithms
myths.reality: Solution Architect interviews focus on system design, cloud services, and communication skills. No LeetCode grinding required. Your real-world experience matters more.
Your TCS, Infosys, Wipro, or Cognizant experience is valuable. You've worked on real enterprise systems, client requirements, and production deployments. That's exactly what SA roles need.

myths.myth: I'm too old / It's too late
myths.reality: Solution Architect is a senior role. Your 10+ years of experience is an asset, not a liability. Companies want architects who've seen real production systems fail and recover.

myths.myth: I need to know everything about cloud
myths.reality: You need depth in ONE cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) and breadth across core services. Start with fundamentals, get one certification, and build from there.

roadmap.title: From Engineer to Solution Architect
roadmap.subtitle: A practical 6-month journey
roadmap.description: This roadmap is designed for working professionals. 1-2 hours daily is enough. No need to quit your job.

phases.title: Master the Fundamentals
phases.description: Before cloud, you need rock-solid basics. Most candidates skip this and struggle later.
phases.milestone: Can explain how a web request travels from browser to server and back

phases.title: Cloud Certification (Pick ONE)
phases.description: Get your first cloud certification. This validates your knowledge and opens doors.
tips: Don't just pass - understand the 'why' behind each service
Do hands-on labs, not just theory
Build at least 3 small projects during prep

phases.title: System Design Mastery
phases.description: Learn to architect real-world systems. This is where interviews are won or lost.

framework.name: IFRAILT
framework.description: My proven 8-step framework for any system design question

phases.milestone: Can design URL shortener, chat system, and notification service end-to-end

phases.title: Behavioral & Communication
phases.description: Solution Architects talk to executives, not just engineers. Communication is 50% of the job.
skills: Explaining technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
phases.tip: Prepare 15-20 stories from your career mapped to common behavioral questions
phases.milestone: Can explain complex architectures to a non-technical person in 5 minutes

phases.title: Mock Interviews & Application
activities: Get feedback from someone who's been through it
Apply to 20-30 SA roles (mix of FAANG and others)
phases.milestone: Receive interview calls and convert at least one to an offer

interviewFAQs.title: Solution Architect Interview Questions
interviewFAQs.subtitle: Master these concepts before your interview

questions.question: What is Amazon EC2 / Azure Virtual Machine?
questions.answer: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) is virtualization of computers on cloud. It's an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering where you can install applications and OS. It virtualizes storage, network, and CPU using hypervisors. You control the OS, patching, and scaling.

questions.question: What is Auto Scaling and why is it important?
questions.answer: Auto Scaling automatically adjusts compute capacity based on demand. You define: Desired Capacity (normal state), Minimum Capacity (floor), Maximum Size (ceiling), and scaling triggers (e.g., CPU > 75%). It enables cost optimization (pay only for what you use) and high availability (handle traffic spikes automatically).

questions.question: What is a Load Balancer? What types exist?
questions.answer: Load Balancer distributes traffic across multiple servers for high availability and performance. Network Load Balancer (Layer 4): Fast, looks at TCP headers, good for high-performance needs. Application Load Balancer (Layer 7): Smart routing, SSL termination, cookie-based sessions, ideal for web applications and microservices.

questions.question: What is DNS and what are key record types?
questions.answer: DNS (Domain Name System) maps IP addresses to user-friendly names - the phonebook of the internet. Key records: A Record (name to IPv4), AAAA Record (name to IPv6), CNAME (domain to domain alias), MX Record (email routing). You can route traffic based on geography, latency, or weight.

questions.question: What is DHCP?
questions.answer: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automatically assigns IP addresses to devices. Process: Device sends DHCP Discover (broadcast), DHCP servers respond with DHCP Offer, device sends DHCP Request to preferred server, server sends DHCP Acknowledgement. Essential for managing large networks (imagine manually assigning IPs to 300K systems!).

questions.question: What is CIDR and why does it matter?
questions.answer: Classless Inter-Domain Routing replaces old classful IP addressing. Format: 192.168.1.0/24 where /24 indicates 24 bits for network, 8 bits for hosts. Allows flexible subnet sizing - you're not stuck with Class A (16M hosts) or Class C (254 hosts). Critical for cloud VPC/VNet design.

questions.question: What is VLAN and VLAN Trunking?
questions.answer: VLAN (Virtual LAN) segments a physical switch into logical switches for security isolation - keep Finance separate from HR on same network. VLAN Trunking connects VLANs across switches using IEEE 802.1Q tags. In cloud, your express route/direct connect uses VLAN tags to keep your traffic separate from other customers.

questions.question: What is IAM?
questions.answer: Identity and Access Management handles Authentication (who are you?) and Authorization (what can you do?). Users get assigned roles with specific permissions to access protected resources. Also provides audit logging of all user activities. Foundation of cloud security - principle of least privilege.

questions.question: What is the difference between Symmetric and Asymmetric encryption?
questions.answer: Symmetric: Same key for encryption and decryption. Fast but key distribution is a problem. Asymmetric: Public key encrypts, private key decrypts (or vice versa for signing). Slower but solves key distribution. In practice, use asymmetric to exchange symmetric keys, then symmetric for data.

questions.question: What is a DDoS attack and how do you prevent it?
questions.answer: Distributed Denial of Service floods your servers with malicious requests until they can't serve legitimate users. Prevention: AWS Shield/Azure DDoS Protection/CloudFlare, Auto-scaling to absorb traffic, Rate limiting, WAF rules, Geographic blocking. Defense in depth is key.

questions.question: What is a Man-in-the-Middle (MiTM) attack?
questions.answer: Attacker intercepts communication between two parties, can eavesdrop or inject false information. Prevention: Use HTTPS/TLS (port 443), VPN for sensitive connections, Certificate pinning, Verify SSL certificates. Tools like Wireshark can be used legitimately or maliciously.

questions.question: How would you secure a cloud environment?
questions.answer: Follow Defense in Depth - multiple layers: 1) Physical security (cloud provider handles), 2) IAM with least privilege, 3) DDoS protection + Firewall at perimeter, 4) IDS/IPS for threat detection, 5) NSG for network segmentation, 6) WAF for application protection, 7) Data encryption at rest and in transit. Each layer adds security.

questions.question: What is the difference between IDS and IPS?
questions.answer: IDS (Intrusion Detection System): Monitors and logs alerts for later analysis. Reactive - you investigate after detection. IPS (Intrusion Prevention System): Actively blocks threats (blocks IPs, drops packets). Proactive but risk of false positives blocking legitimate traffic.

questions.question: What is caching and how does it work?
questions.answer: Caching stores frequently accessed data closer to the user. Flow: Request checks cache first, if miss then fetches from DB and caches result. Benefits: Reduced latency, lower database load, improved performance. Set TTL (Time To Live) to keep data fresh. Examples: Redis, Memcached, CDN caching.

questions.question: What is a message queue (SQS)?
questions.answer: Message queues decouple components for independent scaling and reliability. Producer puts message in queue, consumer processes when ready. Benefits: Handle traffic spikes (queue buffers), retry failed processing, scale producer/consumer independently. AWS SQS, Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ are common choices.

questions.question: What is an API Gateway and why use it?
questions.answer: API Gateway is a single entry point for all API calls. Benefits over plain load balancer: Authentication & authorization, API key management, Rate limiting/throttling, Request/response transformation, Caching, Analytics and monitoring. Essential for microservices architecture.

questions.question: Hybrid Cloud vs Full Cloud - when to use each?
questions.answer: Hybrid: On-premise + cloud connected. Use when: regulatory requirements, existing datacenter investment, ultra-low latency needs, gradual migration. Full Cloud: Everything in cloud. Use when: new company (no legacy), need maximum agility, limited capital for hardware, global scale requirements. Most enterprises are hybrid.

questions.question: How should I approach any technical question?
questions.answer: Use the 4-part framework: 1) WHAT is the technology? (definition), 2) HOW does it work? (mechanism), 3) WHY would you use it? (benefits, use cases), 4) HOW do you architect it? (implementation patterns). This structure shows deep understanding, not just memorization.

questions.question: What does a Solution Architect actually do?
questions.answer: Three core roles: 1) Business Strategist - understand business goals and translate to technical solutions, 2) Advisor - guide teams on best practices and trade-offs, 3) Designer - create architectures that meet requirements. You speak the language of CEO, CIO, CFO AND engineers.

questions.question: What is a Firewall and how does it work?
questions.answer: Firewall protects your network perimeter by blocking unauthorized traffic based on policies. It's stateful - tracks connections so return traffic for your requests is allowed. Default: block all inbound, allow outbound + related return traffic. Configure rules based on IP, port, protocol.
